title: Generics: typed collections, wildcards and type erasure

videos.script: Every collection so far carried a type in angle brackets. This lesson is about what those brackets buy, and what they cost. {{raw}} It starts without them. A list of titles with a year slipped in by mistake. The program compiles, runs, and fails seven lines from the mistake. {{typed}} Add the type, and the same mistake becomes a compile error, on the right line, before anything runs. {{generic}} Then you write your own. A box for any type, and a method that finds the largest of anything comparable. {{wildcards}} Then a surprise. A list of integers is not a list of numbers, and there is a good reason. Wildcards are how a method says it only reads. {{erasure}} Last, where the types go at run time. Nowhere. The compiler checks them, writes the casts for you, and throws the brackets away.
